title: oovi
author: Brahimi Oussama
body: Your own team of AI on your desktop

draft.why: Launch day thread with founder engagement; desktop AI team positioning could serve B2B SaaS users, and a sharp question can surface who the product targets.
options: Congrats on the launch! Curious who you picture as the first user here: is this aimed at solo founders juggling multiple roles, or small teams augmenting what they already have? The answer changes a lot about how the first-run experience should introduce each AI 'teammate'.

Big milestone, well done. Reading 'your own team of AI on your desktop' I wonder if the strongest positioning is actually the desktop part rather than the team part, since privacy and local control are a sharper hook than another multi-agent pitch. Have you tested which framing resonates more with early signups?

title: Omi CLI
author: Om Prakash Sahoo
body: AI coding agents that work while you're away.

draft.why: PH launch in the hot dev tools space; founders here often need landing page and onboarding design help soon after launch.
options: Congrats on the launch! Curious who you built this for first: solo devs who want to queue up tasks overnight, or teams that want agents picking up backlog tickets? The answer changes a lot about how I'd expect the first-run experience to work.

Nice launch. Quick question on positioning: are you framing Omi as a replacement for pairing with an agent live, or as a second shift that hands you PRs to review in the morning? The tagline suggests the latter, and that seems like the stronger story if the review handoff is smooth.
